body:
Fixes #19

Slider changes previously wrote to browser history on every input; Safari's quota exception could remove the editor. History now updates after release and 400 ms of quiet, with bounded retries and exception handling. Preview and share links update immediately. Other history-writing paths receive the same exception protection.

- Fixed self-reference leaving/entering angles, curvature and bend. Hide controls that cannot affect the current network.
- Added independent reference gaps and symmetric start/end/middle marker sizes, angles, tangent/sideways offsets and rotations. Optional cuts on either side of the middle support open rings; the default line stays continuous.
- Applied the requested editor defaults with rotation still zero, while preserving gallery/rain geometry and the gallery preset.
- Added square, hexagonal, dice, playing-card, sunflower and deterministic D3 force placement. Automatic placement uses a circle for 1–4 links. Removed the nine-link limit throughout notations, editing, colours, turns, URLs and exports; large indices/counts remain exact.
- Fixed Safari image clipboard activation by passing a PNG promise to `ClipboardItem` during the click. Native sharing prepares images in advance and retains synchronous link sharing while preparation is pending. Unsupported clipboard capabilities expose download/selectable-link alternatives.
- Corrected large-number fields overflowing their mobile panel and coalesced native-share image rendering during rapid edits.

## Reproduction and tests

The retained [reproduction experiment](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/experiments/issue-19-reproduce.mjs) injects a bounded history quota and records the original blank screen. Failing tests were recorded before each correction; the [case study](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/docs/case-studies/issue-19/README.md) maps every issue requirement to implementation and evidence, including source data, primary-source research, alternatives and default-off diagnostics.

- Unit coverage includes all 4,181 networks with 1–3 links, self-reference controls, marker symmetry, exact cubic cuts, interaction timing, clipboard/share activation, eight placement modes at eleven sizes, and all notation round trips at 10/37/100 links.
- Browser regressions cover 120-event drags, repeated releases, injected history failure/recovery, both complete issue URLs, actual PNG clipboard writes, image downloads, seven distinct layouts, shared-URL reloads and a 100-link touch editor. Existing gallery/editor/export regressions run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in CI.
- Local checks: ESLint, Prettier, file limits, secret scanning, all 682 unit tests, production build, all 120 CV PDFs and a dependency audit with zero vulnerabilities. Browser engines run sequentially locally; CI preserves screenshots and result JSON for each engine.

Final validation: [CI run 40131510761](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/actions/runs/40131510761) passes on the published head `49a22927e75bb29e1806a69c8f2c22ca25311853`: lint, repository checks, all three browser engines, 682 unit tests, production build, all 120 CV PDFs and the Pages artifact. Deployment is intentionally skipped for pull requests. The passing implementation run’s raw logs and browser artifacts are archived in the case study.

Touch tests use browser emulation; operating-system share sheets use gesture-sensitive component tests. The case study records these verification limits. Linux WebKit r2370 has a confirmed upstream backdrop-filter regression ([Playwright #43426](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/43426), [WebKit 327850](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=327850)); bounded probes reproduce it and verify the documented stable Playwright 1.63.0 pin with the unchanged glass gallery. Full browser suites remain enabled for all three engines; CI runs them on separate runners.

## Before and after

History quota: reproduced blank screen, then the editor surviving a rejected history write:

![Before: blank editor](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/docs/case-studies/issue-19/screenshots/before-history-error.png?raw=true)
![After: usable editor](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/docs/case-studies/issue-19/screenshots/chromium-after-history-error.png?raw=true)

Optional ring cuts and independent marker offsets:

![Ring cuts and markers](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/docs/case-studies/issue-19/screenshots/chromium-ring-and-offsets.png?raw=true)

Physical placement for 17 links:

![Force placement](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/docs/case-studies/issue-19/screenshots/chromium-layout-force.png?raw=true)

Large-number mobile fields before and after:

![Before: clipped fields](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/docs/case-studies/issue-19/screenshots/before-mobile-large.png?raw=true)
![After: fields fit](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-19-8244f16d7529/docs/case-studies/issue-19/screenshots/chromium-mobile-100-links.png?raw=true)
title: Fix network editor stability and expand geometry and link placements
